item.title: Undertone 1.39.3
item.description:
• The follow-up after a meeting now shows its formatting (bold headings, italics, links) instead of raw Slack or Markdown markers, and stays editable.
  • Copy puts it on the clipboard as formatted text, so pasting into Slack, Mail or Docs keeps the bold and links.

Undertone 1.39.2

  • Prep in Ask now starts from everything the meeting's Brief has: the talking points, cited facts, open decisions and prep notes, then adds anything new. Asking "prep me for…" or "Elaborate" no longer gives a thinner answer than the Brief.
  • Meetings you organize are recognised as yours on Google and Exchange calendars, so "I'm presenting" turns on by itself (from 1.39.1).

Undertone 1.39.1

  • Meetings you organize are now recognised as yours on Google and Exchange calendars too, so "I'm presenting" turns on by itself and the slides get made without a click. You can still switch it off for any meeting.

Undertone 1.39.0

  • Talking points before every meeting, without a click. Half an hour before a meeting, Undertone writes a full talking-points document: what to say in order with time for each part, the evidence with real ticket keys, numbers and dates, the decisions needed and who owns them, the timeline, and a close. Every fact names its source.
  • Memory first, then your sources. Undertone checks its own memory (past meetings, recaps, tasks, glossary, what you told Ask) first, then searches every source you've connected, such as Granola, Jira, Slack, Notion, Linear, Confluence or Drive. It only reads; it never posts or edits anything.
  • Prep notes for you. Each document ends with the objections to expect and suggested answers, plus loose ends to tidy up first, like tickets still in Backlog or unanswered threads.
  • Slides when you present. For meetings you organize, or when you switch on "I'm presenting", a short slide deck made from the talking points is waiting in Artifacts. Present it or export it from there.
  • Kept up to date. If the meeting moves, the invite changes or something new comes up in Undertone, the talking points are rewritten on their own, at most twice per meeting, so credits aren't wasted. Prep questions now come from the talking points.

Undertone 1.38.3

  • Answer cards in job interviews. What you tell Ask about a meeting (job description, company, your résumé) now feeds the answer cards during the call. An interview on a personal calendar gets cards too, drawn only from what you told Ask, never from work tools or other workspaces.
  • Interview answers from your own background. For "tell me about a time…", "how would you…" or "introduce yourself", cards suggest an example from your résumé and how it fits the role.
